short: The opening series of major clashes between French and German armies, resulting in immense casualties and a French retreat.
full:
On 7 August 1914, French forces launched an offensive into Alsace, marking the beginning of the Battle of the Frontiers. Over the next month, the heavily outnumbered French armies collided with the advancing German right wing across a series of engagements in Lorraine, the Ardennes, and along the Belgian border. The French reliance on spirited infantry charges proved disastrous against German artillery and machine guns.

By early September, the French armies had suffered over a quarter of a million casualties, including 27,000 killed on a single day. The devastating losses forced a general retreat toward the Marne River, setting the stage for the dramatic defensive stand that would ultimately halt the German advance and dictate the next four years of trench warfare.
